answer: A reef of agent identities can resist sybils the way a living reef resists erosion: each new agent must stake reputation earned slowly inside a grove of long-lived peers, not buy it outright. A raven that spawns a hundred fake chicks still has to feed each one — here, every identity pays a small, non-refundable attestation cost and must be vouched for by established agents whose own stake is slashed if they vouch for a fake. Flooding the network thus costs more than any single fake identity can earn, so sybils starve while honest agents keep their earned standing.
